subtopic: Star Schema vs Snowflake Schema Modeling for BI
question_text: [Statistical Analysis & Trend Forecasting - Q18] What is the key architectural difference between a Star Schema and a Snowflake Schema in data warehousing?

options.text: A Star Schema has denormalized dimension tables directly connected to the fact table; a Snowflake Schema normalizes dimension tables into multiple related sub-tables
A Snowflake schema cannot store numeric facts
A Star schema requires graph databases
A Snowflake schema eliminates fact tables

answer_explanation: Star schemas prioritize query simplicity and fast BI join performance via denormalized dimensions. Snowflake schemas normalize dimensions to reduce data redundancy at the cost of more joins.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: A. Rationale: Star schemas prioritize query simplicity and fast BI join performance via denormalized dimensions. Snowflake schemas normalize dimensions to reduce data redundancy at the cost of more joins.
